gaps.sentence: He ___ her on her excellent presentation.
gaps.explanation: 'Compliment somebody on something' means to praise; 'complement' means to go well with.

gaps.sentence: She has lived in this street ___ 2015.
gaps.hint: starting point of a period up to now
gaps.explanation: 'Since' is used with a point in time when the situation started and continues; 'for' is used with a length of time.

gaps.sentence: This small car is very ___ to run.
gaps.explanation: 'Economical' means costing little or saving money; 'economic' relates to trade, industry or the economy.

gaps.hint: noun meaning a moral rule; fixed phrase 'on principle'
gaps.explanation: 'On principle' means because of a moral belief; 'principal' means main or the head of a school.

gaps.sentence: Teenagers ___ hours every day on social media.
gaps.hint: to use time or money on something (neutral)
gaps.explanation: 'Spend time/money on something' is the neutral verb for using time or money; 'waste' implies useless use.

gaps.sentence: Tax is calculated on your total annual ___.
gaps.hint: all the money you receive from every source
gaps.explanation: 'Income' is all the money you receive from work, investments, rent and so on during a period.

gaps.sentence: The two leaders signed a ___ peace agreement.
gaps.hint: important enough to be remembered in history
gaps.explanation: 'Historic' means important or famous in history; 'historical' just means connected with the past or the study of history.

gaps.hint: the standard verb with television and sport
gaps.explanation: 'Watch television' is the fixed collocation; 'look' needs 'at', and 'see television' is not used.
